# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

```
Supported sub-commands:
	check - run linter over specified targets
		$ go-critic check -help
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
	version - print linter version
		$ go-critic version
	doc - get installed checkers documentation
		$ go-critic doc -help
		$ go-critic doc
		$ go-critic doc checkerName
```

### Examples

```bash
# Runs all stable checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check fmt

# Run all stable checkers on `pkg1` and `pkg2`
go-critic check pkg1 pkg2

# Run all stable checkers on `fmt` package and configure rangeExprCopy checker
go-critic check -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold 128 fmt

# Runs specified checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check -enable elseif,paramName fmt

# Run all stable checkers on current dir and all its children recursively:
go-critic check ./...

# Like above, but without `appendAssign` check:
go-critic check -disable=appendAssign ./...

# Run all stable checkers on `foo.go` file:
go-critic check foo.go

# Run stable diagnostics over `strings` package:
go-critic check -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental' strings

# Run all stable and non-opinionated checks:
go-critic check -enableAll -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./src/...
```

> To get a list of available checker parameters, run `go-critic doc <checkerName>`.

### Checker Tags

In place of a single name, **tag** can be used. Tag is a named checkers group.

Tags:

* `#diagnostic` - kind of checks that detect various errors in code
* `#style` - kind of checks that find style issues in code
* `#performance` - kind of checks that detect potential performance issues in code
* `#experimental` - check is under testing and development. Disabled by default
* `#opinionated` - check can be unwanted for some people. Disabled by default
* `#security` - kind of checks that find security issues in code. Disabled by default

## Documentation

For complete documentation and a full list of checkers, visit [go-critic.com](https://go-critic.com/overview).

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

```
Supported sub-commands:
	check - run linter over specified targets
		$ go-critic check -help
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
	version - print linter version
		$ go-critic version
	doc - get installed checkers documentation
		$ go-critic doc -help
		$ go-critic doc
		$ go-critic doc checkerName
```

### Examples

```bash
# Runs all stable checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check fmt

# Run all stable checkers on `pkg1` and `pkg2`
go-critic check pkg1 pkg2

# Run all stable checkers on `fmt` package and configure rangeExprCopy checker
go-critic check -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold 128 fmt

# Runs specified checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check -enable elseif,paramName fmt

# Run all stable checkers on current dir and all its children recursively:
go-critic check ./...

# Like above, but without `appendAssign` check:
go-critic check -disable=appendAssign ./...

# Run all stable checkers on `foo.go` file:
go-critic check foo.go

# Run stable diagnostics over `strings` package:
go-critic check -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental' strings

# Run all stable and non-opinionated checks:
go-critic check -enableAll -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./src/...
```

> To get a list of available checker parameters, run `go-critic doc <checkerName>`.

### Checker Tags

In place of a single name, **tag** can be used. Tag is a named checkers group.

Tags:

* `#diagnostic` - kind of checks that detect various errors in code
* `#style` - kind of checks that find style issues in code
* `#performance` - kind of checks that detect potential performance issues in code
* `#experimental` - check is under testing and development. Disabled by default
* `#opinionated` - check can be unwanted for some people. Disabled by default
* `#security` - kind of checks that find security issues in code. Disabled by default

## Documentation

For complete documentation and a full list of checkers, visit [go-critic.com](https://go-critic.com/overview).

rangeExprCopy checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [performance]

Detects expensive copies of `for` loop range expressions.

Suggests to use pointer to array to avoid the copy using `&` on range expression.

Non-compliant code:
var xs [2048]byte
for _, x := range xs { // Copies 2048 bytes
	// Loop body.
}

Compliant code:
var xs [2048]byte
for _, x := range &xs { // No copy
	// Loop body.
}

See Go issue for details: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/15812.

Checker parameters:

func(x int) int { return fn(x) }

Compliant code:
fn

unnamedResult checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [style opinionated experimental]

Detects unnamed results that may benefit from names.

Non-compliant code:
func f() (float64, float64)

Compliant code:
func f() (x, y float64)

  -@unnamedResult.checkExported bool
    	whether to check exported functions (default false)

=== unnecessaryBlock.txt ===
unnecessaryBlock checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [style opinionated experimental]

Detects unnecessary braced statement blocks.

Non-compliant code:
x := 1
{
	print(x)
}

Compliant code:
x := 1
print(x)

=== unnecessaryDefer.txt ===
unnecessaryDefer checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [diagnostic experimental]

Detects redundantly deferred calls.

Non-compliant code:
func() {
	defer os.Remove(filename)
}

Compliant code:
func() {
	os.Remove(filename)
}

=== unslice.txt ===
unslice checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [style]

Detects slice expressions that can be simplified to sliced expression itself.

Non-compliant code:
copy(b[:], values...)

Compliant code:
copy(b, values...)

=== valSwap.txt ===
valSwap checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [style]

Detects value swapping code that are not using parallel assignment.

Non-compliant code:
*tmp = *x; *x = *y; *y = *tmp

Compliant code:
*x, *y = *y, *x

=== weakCond.txt ===
weakCond checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers

xs != nil && xs[0] != nil

len(xs) != 0 && xs[0] != nil

whyNoLint checker documentation

//nolint // reason

wg.Done()

mapKey checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [diagnostic]

Detects suspicious map literal keys.

Non-compliant code:
_ = map[string]int{
	"foo": 1,
	"bar ": 2,
}

Compliant code:
_ = map[string]int{
	"foo": 1,
	"bar": 2,
}

=====
defaultCaseOrder checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [style]

Detects when default case in switch isn't on 1st or last position.

Non-compliant code:
switch {
case x > y:
	// ...
default: // <- not the best position
	// ...
case x == 10:
	// ...
}

Compliant code:
switch {
case x > y:
	// ...
case x == 10:
	// ...
default: // <- last case (could also be the first one)
	// ...
}

deprecatedComment checker documentation
URL: https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/checkers
Tags: [diagnostic]

Detects malformed 'deprecated' doc-comments.

func FuncOld() int

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

const versionStr = "v0.0.0-SNAPSHOT"

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "no args provided")
		return
	}
	cmd := os.Args[1]
	args := os.Args[2:]
	switch cmd {
	case "help":
		printHelp()
	case "version":
		printVersion()
	case "doc":
		runDoc(args)
	case "check":
		runCheck(args)
	default:
		handleUnknownCommand(cmd)
	}
}

func printHelp() {
	fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, "Usage:\n\n    go-critic <command> [arguments...]\n\nThe commands are:\n\n    check             run linter over specified targets\n    doc               get installed checkers documentation\n    help              shows help message\n    version           shows version of the application\n\nVersion: "+versionStr+"\n\n")
}

func printVersion() {
	fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, "go-critic version: "+versionStr+"\n\n")
}

func handleUnknownCommand(cmd string) {
	if cmd == "--help" {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "\"%s\" unknown command, did you mean \"help\"?\nRun \"go-critic help\" for usage.\n\n", cmd)
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "\"%s\" unknown command\nRun \"go-critic help\" for usage.\n\n", cmd)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "no such command \"%s\"\n", cmd)
}

package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
)

func runDoc(args []string) {
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("go-critic", flag.ContinueOnError)
	// No flags for doc; output to stderr
	fs.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
	// Custom usage? Use default which prints "Usage of go-critic:\n"
	err := fs.Parse(args)
	if err != nil {
		// flag package already printed err + usage to stderr
		// Now print err again and exit 0 (as observed)
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(0)
		return
	}
	rest := fs.Args()
	if len(rest) > 1 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "expected 0 or 1 positional arguments")
		os.Exit(1)
		return
	}
	if len(rest) == 0 {
		// list all checkers: name + tags
		for _, name := range checkerList {
			tags := checkerTags[name]
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stdout, "%s [%s]\n", name, strings.Join(tags, " "))
		}
		return
	}
	name := rest[0]
	text, ok := checkerDocText[name]
	if !ok {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "checker with name %q not found\n", name)
		os.Exit(1)
		return
	}
	fmt.Fprint(os.Stdout, text)
}

func parseList(s string) []string {
	if s == "" {
		return nil
	}
	parts := strings.Split(s, ",")
	var out []string
	for _, p := range parts {
		p = strings.TrimSpace(p)
		if p != "" {
			out = append(out, p)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func selectCheckers(cf *checkFlags) (map[string]bool, []string, bool) {

		if cf.enableAll {

		}
		tags := checkerTags[name]
		for _, e := range enableList {
			if strings.HasPrefix(e, "#") {
				tag := strings.TrimPrefix(e, "#")
				for _, t := range tags {
					if t == tag {
						return true
					}
				}
			} else {
				if e == name {
					return true
				}
			}
		}
		return false
	}
	// Helper to find disable reason (name takes precedence over tag)
	findDisable := func(name string) (string, bool) {
		// Check name first
		for _, d := range disableList {
			if !strings.HasPrefix(d, "#") && d == name {
				return "name", true
			}
		}
		// Then tags
		tags := checkerTags[name]
		for _, d := range disableList {
			if strings.HasPrefix(d, "#") {
				tag := strings.TrimPrefix(d, "#")
				for _, t := range tags {
					if t == tag {
						return tag, true
					}
				}
			}
		}
		return "", false
	}

	for _, name := range checkerList {

			debugLines = append(debugLines, fmt.Sprintf("\tdebug: %s: not enabled by name or tag (-enable)", name))

		// Would be enabled, check disable
		if tagOrName, ok := findDisable(name); ok {
			if tagOrName == "name" {
				debugLines = append(debugLines, fmt.Sprintf("\tdebug: %s: disabled by name (-disable)", name))
			} else {
				debugLines = append(debugLines, fmt.Sprintf("\tdebug: %s: disabled by %q tag (-disable)", name, tagOrName))

		enabled[name] = true
	}

	// Let's reorder.
	var first, second []string
	// Need to separate: enabled lines go to second, others to first
	// Our debugLines currently interleaved; split them
	for _, l := range debugLines {
		if strings.Contains(l, " is enabled") {
			second = append(second, l)
		} else {
			first = append(first, l)
		}
	}
	debugLines = append(first, second...)

		return enabled, debugLines, true
	}
	return enabled, debugLines, false

)

func formatLocation(pos token.Position, cf *checkFlags) string {
	filename := pos.Filename
	if cf.shorterErrLocation {
		// Try GOROOT/GOPATH replacement
		goroot := runtime.GOROOT()
		if goroot != "" && strings.HasPrefix(filename, goroot) {
			rest := strings.TrimPrefix(filename, goroot)
			// Ensure leading slash?
			filename = "$GOROOT" + rest
		} else {
			// GOPATH: from env or default
			gopath := os.Getenv("GOPATH")
			if gopath == "" {
				// Try go env? Use home/go
				if home, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil {
					gopath = filepath.Join(home, "go")
				}
			}
			// GOPATH may contain multiple paths separated by :
			for _, gp := range strings.Split(gopath, string(os.PathListSeparator)) {
				if gp != "" && strings.HasPrefix(filename, gp) {
					rest := strings.TrimPrefix(filename, gp)
					filename = "$GOPATH" + rest
					break
				}
			}
			// If not replaced, try relative to cwd
			if !strings.HasPrefix(filename, "$") {
				cwd, err := os.Getwd()
				if err == nil {
					// If filename is absolute, try rel
					abs := filename
					if !filepath.IsAbs(abs) {
						// Make absolute first
						abs = filepath.Join(cwd, abs)
					}
					rel, err := filepath.Rel(cwd, abs)
					if err == nil && rel != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) && rel != ".." {
						// Prefix with ./ if not already starting with ./
						if !strings.HasPrefix(rel, "./") && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, "../") {
							rel = "./" + rel
						}
						filename = rel
					} else {
						// Outside cwd, keep absolute (already absolute)
						filename = abs
					}
				}
			}
		}
		// If filename is still relative without ./ prefix, add ./?
		// For file targets like "a.go" parsed as absolute, above already handled.
		// But if filename was originally relative (shouldn't happen since we use absolute), handle.
		if !filepath.IsAbs(filename) && !strings.HasPrefix(filename, "./") && !strings.HasPrefix(filename, "../") && !strings.HasPrefix(filename, "$") {
			filename = "./" + filename
		}
	} else {
		// shorter false: always absolute
		if !filepath.IsAbs(filename) {
			cwd, _ := os.Getwd()
			filename = filepath.Join(cwd, filename)
		}
		filename = filepath.Clean(filename)
	}
	return filename + ":" + itoa(pos.Line) + ":" + itoa(pos.Column)
}

func itoa(i int) string {
	// fast int to string
	if i == 0 {
		return "0"
	}
	neg := false
	if i < 0 {
		neg = true
		i = -i
	}
	var buf [20]byte
	pos := len(buf)
	for i > 0 {
		pos--
		buf[pos] = byte('0' + i%10)
		i /= 10
	}
	if neg {
		pos--
		buf[pos] = '-'
	}
	return string(buf[pos:])
}

func checkElseif(cf *checkFlags, fset *token.FileSet, f *ast.File) []Warning {

		}

		if !ok || elseBlock == nil {

		if !ok {

			if len(ifStmt.Body.List) == 1 {
				if _, ok := ifStmt.Body.List[0].(*ast.IfStmt); ok {

				}
			}
		}
		// Report at else block's Lbrace? Use elseBlock.Lbrace position

func checkAssignOp(cf *checkFlags, fset *token.FileSet, f *ast.File) []Warning {

		assign, ok := n.(*ast.AssignStmt)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		if assign.Tok != token.ASSIGN || len(assign.Lhs) != 1 || len(assign.Rhs) != 1 {
			return true
		}
		lhs := assign.Lhs[0]
		rhs, ok := assign.Rhs[0].(*ast.BinaryExpr)
		if !ok {
			return true
		}
		// Check lhs == rhs.X (same expr)
		if !astEqual(lhs, rhs.X) {
			return true
		}
		lhsStr := nodeString(fset, lhs)
		// Need to handle different ops
		op := rhs.Op
		var suggestion string
		orig := nodeString(fset, assign)

			} else {
				suggestion = lhsStr + " -= " + nodeString(fset, rhs.Y)
			}
		case token.MUL:
			suggestion = lhsStr + " *= " + nodeString(fset, rhs.Y)
		case token.QUO:
			suggestion = lhsStr + " /= " + nodeString(fset, rhs.Y)
		case token.REM:
			suggestion = lhsStr + " %= " + nodeString(fset, rhs.Y)
		case token.AND:

		case token.OR:

func sortWarnings(ws []Warning) {
	sort.Slice(ws, func(i, j int) bool {
		if ws[i].Pos.Filename != ws[j].Pos.Filename {
			return ws[i].Pos.Filename < ws[j].Pos.Filename
		}
		if ws[i].Pos.Line != ws[j].Pos.Line {
			return ws[i].Pos.Line < ws[j].Pos.Line

		if ws[i].Pos.Column != ws[j].Pos.Column {

		}
		return ws[i].Text < ws[j].Text
